chunks: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Surely Allah the Exalted sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) to the Jinn and humans generally. And after him there were twelve successors (Wasiyy), some of whom have preceded us (passed away) and some of whom remain. Every successor followed the established practice (Sunnah). The successors who came after Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) were upon the practice of the successors of Isa (Jesus) until Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and they were twelve. And the Commander of the Faithful (Ali) (peace be upon him) was upon the practice of the Messiah (Jesus).

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title for Imam Ali
key_terms.وَصِيٌّ: Successor or heir, specifically referring to the Imams in this context

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the number twelve in Shia Imamate theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* firmly establishes the doctrine of the Twelve Imams as divinely appointed successors (Wasiyy) to the Prophet, extending the lineage to the present day. It draws a significant theological parallel between the succession of Muhammad and that of Jesus, highlighting that Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib followed the tradition of the Messiah, thereby linking the prophetic and imamic lineages through a consistent pattern of twelve leaders.
